lens: Security review — attack-surface delta, OWASP classes, DoS/data-integrity/correctness
answer: From an F7 lens these four sub-checks are read-only filesystem scanners over trusted workspace-owned directories, so attack-surface delta is minimal: no network, no eval, no shell-out, no user-controlled paths (all joined from string literals). However, the design fails-open on every I/O error (read_dir/read_to_string Err is silently swallowed via if let Ok), and the consensus-debate evidence gate is trivially bypassable because it uses substring search on raw JSON text rather than parsed structural matching — a contributor can either fail-open by corrupting a file or bypass the gate by ensuring `meta_review_triggered: true` never appears as a literal substring (e.g., spacing variants, nested string values, comments). Day-1 severity is bounded because all checks are ReportOnly and findings non-blocking, but the bypass-by-construction pattern must be hardened before any of these are promoted to Error severity.
key_claims: All path inputs are derived from ctx.workspace_root.join(<string literal>); no user-controlled path segments, so classic path-traversal (../) is not reachable through this code.

Symlink risk is present but low: std::fs::read_dir/read_to_string follow symlinks by default, so a malicious symlink placed inside scripts/, specs/cross-cutting/, evidence/multispectrum/, evidence/per-change/, or evidence/debate/ could redirect reads to arbitrary files; however, since the read content is only used for counting/substring matching and never executed or echoed verbatim, blast radius is limited to skewed counters and potential DoS via giant target files.

DoS class — unbounded read_to_string: check_scorecard_render and check_consensus_debate_evidence call std::fs::read_to_string with no size cap on each .json file in evidence/multispectrum and evidence/per-change. A single multi-GB JSON file (accidental or malicious) would be fully loaded into RAM, OOMing the CI runner.

DoS class — directory width is bounded only by the filesystem: no per-call entry cap. A pathological evidence/ directory with millions of files would block the lane indefinitely. Recursion depth is NOT a concern because read_dir is non-recursive (single-level).

Data-integrity / trivial-bypass — check_consensus_debate_evidence detects `meta_review_triggered: true` by raw substring scan of the JSON text. This is fooled in both directions: (a) a malicious or careless evidence file embedding that literal substring inside a comment, an unrelated string field, or a nested debate-quote would inflate meta_triggered; (b) a contributor wishing to bypass the gate need only write `"meta_review_triggered"  : true` (extra whitespace), `"meta_review_triggered": True`, or place the flag inside a nested object that serializes with different spacing — all evade both string forms hard-coded at lines 884-885.

Data-integrity — scorecard-render uses the same brittle substring approach (`"change_class_id"` AND `"facets"`); a file containing those literals inside string values (e.g., documentation evidence) is mis-counted as renderable.

Fail-open-on-error — every read_dir and read_to_string error path is silently dropped via `if let Ok(...)`. A permissions error, I/O error, or transient ENOENT on evidence/debate would yield synthesis_present=0 silently, which combined with meta_triggered=0 (also fail-open) means a totally broken evidence tree reports clean.
filter_map(Result::ok) on read_dir entries silently drops any entry whose stat/readdir errors — same fail-open class, hides genuine corruption.
No timeouts apply (no network/process), so the no-connection-timeout anti-pattern is not applicable.

Day-1 severity is bounded: all four checks return Severity::ReportOnly and three of four return NotYetArmed, so a malicious commit cannot block or unblock CI through these paths today — risk is latent until the FixupTasks (F-LANE-RUST-DEFAULT-ENFORCE, F-NAMING-CONVENTION-ENFORCE, F-LANE-SCORECARD-RENDER, F-LANE-DEBATE-SUBCHECK) promote them.
uncertainty_areas: Whether evidence/multispectrum, evidence/per-change, evidence/debate are write-restricted by branch protection or CODEOWNERS — if any unprivileged contributor can land JSON there, the trivial-bypass on substring matching becomes higher severity.
Whether CI runners impose a memory ceiling that would cap the unbounded read_to_string DoS to a contained failure rather than a host crash.

Whether WorkspaceContext.workspace_root is itself derived from any environment variable or CLI flag (not shown in this hunk); if it is, path-injection upstream of these checks could redirect the scans, even though the joined segments are literals.
Whether symlinks are blocked by a pre-existing repo policy or git hook; default git behavior preserves symlinks, and these checks would follow them.

specific_findings.summary: check_consensus_debate_evidence uses substring matching on raw JSON text for the meta_review_triggered gate (lines 884-885); trivially bypassed by whitespace variants, case variants, or embedded string occurrences, and equally trivially false-positived by quoted documentation strings. Once this sub-check is promoted from ReportOnly to Error (per F-LANE-DEBATE-SUBCHECK), a malicious or careless contributor can bypass the consensus-debate evidence requirement.
specific_findings.recommended_action: Replace substring scan with serde_json (or std-only hand-rolled JSON parser already implied by render_report_json) structural parse: parse the object, traverse to the documented key path, and compare against the typed boolean true. Apply the same fix to scorecard-render's `change_class_id`/`facets` substring checks. Add a unit test that asserts `"meta_review_triggered":  true` (extra space) is correctly detected and that an embedded string `"note": "meta_review_triggered: true was discussed"` is NOT.

specific_findings.summary: All four sub-checks silently swallow read_dir and read_to_string errors via `if let Ok(...)` and `filter_map(Result::ok)`. A permissions error, FS corruption, or missing directory yields counters of 0 and a green ReportOnly status — the gate fails open and hides genuine evidence-tree breakage.
specific_findings.recommended_action: Convert each Err branch to push an explicit finding string (e.g., 'failed to read evidence/debate: <io::Error kind>') and set SubCheckStatus::Fail (or at minimum NotYetArmed with the error surfaced). Never let an I/O error produce an empty-but-passing scan.

specific_findings.summary: Unbounded std::fs::read_to_string on every .json file under evidence/multispectrum and evidence/per-change (check_scorecard_render and check_consensus_debate_evidence). A pathological or accidentally-committed multi-GB JSON would OOM the CI runner; no per-file size cap, no streaming reader.
specific_findings.recommended_action: Wrap reads with a size guard (e.g., metadata().len() <= 4 MiB threshold) and skip-with-finding above that. Alternatively use a streaming byte scanner that early-exits once both required substrings are seen. Document the cap in the sub-check rustdoc.

specific_findings.summary: read_dir follows symlinks; a symlink committed under scripts/, specs/cross-cutting/, registries/cross-cutting/, evidence/multispectrum/, evidence/per-change/, or evidence/debate/ would redirect the scan to arbitrary repo paths (or outside the repo). Blast radius is bounded to counter-skewing today because content is never executed, but combined with the substring-bypass finding this becomes an amplification vector.
specific_findings.recommended_action: Use entry.file_type()? and skip is_symlink() entries, or canonicalize and re-check that the path remains under ctx.workspace_root before reading. Add a sub-check finding that enumerates any skipped symlinks so they are auditable rather than silently ignored.

specific_findings.summary: check_naming_convention only scans the top level of four canonical homes (non-recursive read_dir) but the rustdoc implies BNF enforcement over the full canonical tree. Files nested below the top level escape the naming gate entirely — this is a correctness/coverage gap that an attacker could exploit by placing non-conformant names one directory deeper.
specific_findings.recommended_action: Either (a) extend to a depth-bounded walk (depth <= N, N>=2) with a clear cap on entries scanned, or (b) tighten the rustdoc to state explicitly 'top-level only, deep walk arrives with F-NAMING-CONVENTION-ENFORCE'. Pair with the symlink-skip recommendation above to avoid unbounded recursion.

specific_findings.summary: check_naming_convention caps violations.push at 10 (line 792) but still increments scanned; violations 11..N are silently dropped from the findings vector. This is a soft fail-open: the status correctly becomes Fail when any violation exists, but downstream reviewers only see the first 10 names, so a coordinated batch of bad names could hide the worst offenders behind the cap.
specific_findings.recommended_action: Append a final 'and <N-10> more not shown' finding when violations.len() > 10 so the truncation is auditable; consider tracking the total separately from the displayed slice.
